flawed_step: The claim that the stable 2-WL colouring determines the isomorphism type fails immediately. For any strongly regular graph, the initial partition of ordered pairs into equal/adjacent/non-adjacent is already stable. The counts of w with each colour pair (c(u,w),c(w,v)) depend only on (n,k,lambda,mu). So strongly regular graphs with the same parameters get identical stable colour multisets.
counterexample: G = 4x4 rook's graph (vertices (i,j) in {0..3}^2, adjacent iff same row or same column), SRG(16,6,2,2). H = Shrikhande graph, the Cayley graph on Z4xZ4 with connection set {±(1,0),±(0,1),±(1,1)}, also SRG(16,6,2,2). 2-WL: both graphs are stable at the initial colouring, with 16 diagonal, 96 edge and 144 non-edge pairs, so the stable multisets are equal. Not isomorphic: in G every vertex neighbourhood is K3+K3 (rest of row, rest of column). In H the neighbourhood of (0,0) is {(1,0),(3,0),(0,1),(0,3),(1,1),(3,3)}, which induces the 6-cycle (1,0)-(1,1)-(0,1)-(3,0)-(3,3)-(0,3)-(1,0) with no chords (e.g. (1,0)-(3,0) has difference (2,0), not in the set). C6 is not K3+K3.
assessment_summary: False. Non-isomorphic strongly regular graphs with equal parameters are indistinguishable by 2-WL, because the initial pair colouring is already stable and its counts depend only on the parameters. The witness is the 4x4 rook's graph versus the Shrikhande graph, both SRG(16,6,2,2), with vertex neighbourhoods K3+K3 versus C6.
